rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for furniture, places, or clothing that looks worn-out and ragged.

example.english: That old sofa is so shabby that I really don’t want to sit on it.
example.traditional: 嗰張舊梳化殘到直情唔想坐。
example.jyutping: go2 zoeng1 gau6 so1 faa3 caan4 dou3 zik6 cing4 m4 soeng2 co5

rows.note: Use this for a person or behaviour that is mean, nasty, or treats someone badly, rather than for physical shabbiness.

example.english: That was shabby of you, taking someone else’s credit as your own.
example.traditional: 你咁衰，竟然攞人哋份功勞當自己嘅。
example.jyutping: nei5 gam3 seoi1 ging2 jin4 lo2 jan4 dei6 fan2 gung1 lou4 dong1 zi6 gei2 ge3

rows.note: Use this for something of poor quality or work that shows little ability or effort.

example.english: This piece of work is shabby; it’s obvious you didn’t put much effort into it.
example.traditional: 呢份功課做得好差，睇得出你冇乜用心。
example.jyutping: ne1 fan6 gung1 fo3 zou6 dak1 hou2 caa1 tai2 dak1 ceot1 nei5 mou5 mat1 jung6 sam1
